validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/SPEC: real, gas transmission pipeline, confirmed. Read all three cited sources directly (not just the automated checker). dostor.org/4234553 (2022-11-18, 'بتوجيهات من الرئيس السيسى.. تطوير خط «إدكو- أبوحمص» لزيادة صادرات الغاز') states verbatim: 'وجرى تطوير خط فاز «ادكو- أبو حمص» في محافظة البحيرة، لتدعيم الشبكة القومية للقاز بطول ۳۰ كم وقطر ۴۲ بوصة، بتكلفة ۷۳۳ مليون جنيه' (the Idku-Abu Hummus line in Beheira governorate was developed to reinforce the national gas grid, 30km/42in, cost 733M EGP). egy-map.com (sourced 'from the official website of the Presidency') gives an identical description plus 'تاريخ التنفيذ فبراير ۲۰۲۰' (completion date Feb 2020) and status 'تم تنفيذه' (implemented/completed). petro-news.com/95212 (2024-10-10, a roundup of '39 gas projects in Egypt') repeats the identical 30km/42in/733M figures for the same named project. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: these three sources are NOT independent of each other -- all three trace to the same origin, the Egyptian Presidency's official megaprojects database/press material (egy-map explicitly cites 'نقلا من الموقع الرسمي لرئاسة الجمهورية'); this is one lineage restated three times, not 2+ independent corroborations, per the near-requirement. A genuinely separate origin -- GASCO's (Egyptian Natural Gas Company, Egypt's state gas-transmission grid operator) own official pipelines page -- surfaced in a Google search snippet describing 'Edco/Abu-Hommus gas pipeline is 29 km ... 42in diameter ... to transmit gas from north Alex fields ... capacity 35 MSCM/day ... scheduled to be completed and operational in July 2019', which corroborates length/diameter/existence from a second, non-Presidency-database source. However the live URL (http://www.gasco.com.eg/?page_id=5242) now fails to resolve (ConnectTimeout on http, SSLError on https -- site appears to have been restructured; the search engine still has the old page indexed) so it CANNOT be cited as a proposed_ref per the url_verifier requirement -- noting it here as uncited corroboration only, per the no-fabricated-URL rule. Net: length 30km (Presidency lineage) vs 29km (GASCO, uncited) is an immaterial ~3% variance; diameter 42in corroborated by two genuinely distinct origins -- confirmed. Classification (transmission, feeding the national gas grid from field-side production) is correct, not a gathering/plant-internal line. DUPLICATE CHECK: compared against the full 30-row Egypt-gas-operating roster and the 95-feature GulfPub Egypt list -- no other GEM row or GulfPub feature represents this specific Idku-to-Abu-Hummus corridor (the several other Idku-prefixed rows/features -- Idku-Tanta, Idku-Damietta, Rashid-Idku, Simian/Sienna-Idku, Fayoum-Idku -- are all different corridors/endpoints). No duplicate identified. Note for a future dedup pass: the project is explicitly described as an 'ازدواج' (doubling/twinning) of an existing corridor -- i.e. a second parallel pipe alongside a pre-existing line on the same route -- so if GEM ever captures the original (pre-2020) single line under a different name, that would need reconciling against this row; no such row was found in the current roster/GulfPub list, so not flagged as an active duplicate now. Automated ref-checker false negatives worth noting (not real problems): the SegmentCost check flagged '733,000,000' as 'not found' on egy-map.com because the page spells the value as '۷۳۳ مليون جنيه' (733 million pounds, not digit-string '733000000'); the ConstructionYear check similarly flagged '2020' as 'not found' because the page uses Arabic-Indic digits '۲۰۲۰' rather than ASCII '2020'. Both values ARE present on manual read.

validity.researcher_notes: Read the full raw text of the cited dostor.org/4234553 article directly (WebFetch was blocked by a 403, so fetched via curl with a browser UA and parsed the HTML). The article covers TWO separate projects in one piece: (1) 'the Idku-Abu Hummus gas LINE ... 30km/42in, cost 733M EGP' (the pipeline row this shard covers), and separately (2) 'كما تم تطوير مصنع إدكو لإسالة القاز الطبيعي' (the Idku NATURAL GAS LIQUEFACTION PLANT was also developed). The article then states verbatim, describing the LNG PLANT specifically: 'يعمل على مصنع إسالة القاز الطبيعي بإدكو عدد من الشركات وهي الهينة العامة للبترول بنسبة ۱۲%، والشركة المصرية القابضة للقازات الطبيعية "إيجاس" ۱۲%، وشركة بريتش جاز التى استحوذت عليها شركة شل ۳۵.۵%، وشركة بتروناس الماليزية ۳۵.۵%، وشركة إنجى الفرنسية ... ۵%' (the Idku LNG liquefaction plant has several companies working on it: EGPC 12%, EGAS 12%, British Gas [acquired by Shell] 35.5%, Petronas 35.5%, Engie [formerly Gaz de France] 5%). Those exact five owners and exact percentages are what GEM has attached to the PIPELINE row (Owner1='General Petroleum Co' 12%, Owner2='Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co' 12%, Owner3='British Gas' 35.5%, Owner4='Petronas' 35.5%, Owner5='Engie SA' 5%) -- i.e. the ownership structure of a wholly separate asset (the LNG export terminal) has been copy-pasted onto this domestic 30km transmission spur. Independently corroborated: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edku confirms the Idku LNG plant is 'jointly owned by Shell and Petronas' -- the same two majority owners, describing the LNG plant specifically, with no mention of pipeline ownership. The pipeline itself is explicitly a national-gas-grid reinforcement project attributed to Ministry of Petroleum/Presidency directives, which in Egypt's sector structure is normally built/operated by GASCO (Egyptian Natural Gas Company), not by the offshore-field/LNG-plant JV partners -- but I could not find a source naming GASCO specifically for THIS pipeline (only its general remit over the national grid), so I am not proposing a replacement owner value, just flagging the current one as wrong.

validity.recommendation: FuelSource 'Idku Oil Fields' should read 'Idku gas fields' (or similar) -- every source describing this project calls it a gas line moved gas produced from Idku's GAS fields; none mentions oil.
validity.researcher_notes: dostor.org and egy-map.com both state the project's purpose as 'نقل القاز المنتج من حقول إدكو' (transporting the gas produced from Idku FIELDS -- حقول = fields, no qualifier of 'oil'; the whole subject of the sentence and the source document is natural gas). GASCO's own description (search-snippet only, uncited live) calls the source 'north Alex[andria] fields', i.e. the North Alexandria/West Delta Deep Marine gas concessions that come onshore at Idku -- again gas, not oil. 'Idku Oil Fields' as currently written appears to be a mislabeling.

validity.recommendation: StartYear1=2022 (cited to dostor.org, published 2022-11-18) is not actually supported by that article's text -- the article never states a 2022 completion/start date, it simply reports on already-completed infrastructure as of its Nov-2022 publish date. The article's PUBLISH date appears to have been mistaken for a project START year. egy-map.com (sourced from the Presidency's own project database) explicitly gives 'тاريخ التنفيذ فبراير ۲۰۲۰' (completion/implementation date: February 2020) -- recommend StartYear1 ≈ 2020 instead, sourced to egy-map.com; reconsider whether ConstructionYear (currently also 2020, same source) and StartYear1 should be two different years or are duplicating one data point.
validity.researcher_notes: Confirmed by reading egy-map.com's raw page text: 'الحالة: تم تنفيذه ... تاريخ الтنفيذ فبراير ۲۰۲۰' (status: implemented/completed ... implementation date: February 2020). This is consistent with GASCO's own (uncited, dead-link) corporate description that the line was 'scheduled to be completed and operational in July 2019' -- both independently point to a 2019-2020 in-service window, not 2022. Read the full dostor.org article body directly and it contains no year other than the implicit publish date (2022-11-18) and no explicit project-start/completion year at all -- it is a generic 'the Ministry has done a lot under Sisi's directives' piece, so citing it for StartYear1=2022 looks like a date-of-publication/date-of-event conflation.

routes.start_name: Idku, Beheira Governorate (Idku/West Delta Deep Marine gas fields coming onshore near the Idku LNG complex)
routes.corridor_desc: Straight-line distance between the two named towns is ~23km (Idku 31.306N/30.298E per Wikipedia 'Edku' infobox and latitude.to; Abu Hummus 31.101N/30.313E per Wikipedia 'Abu Hummus' infobox), against a stated pipe length of 29-30km -- consistent with a route that doesn't run point-to-point but follows an existing corridor south from the coastal Idku gas/LNG facilities through Beheira farmland toward Abu Hummus, which Wikipedia describes as lying 'between the Cairo-Alexandria Agricultural Road and the El-Mahmoudeya Canal' -- i.e. the road/canal corridor connecting Idku to Damanhur-area towns is the most defensible general path. No actual pipe centerline was sourced; this is a two-point bound (named endpoints only), not a traced route. Do not treat the corridor description as a coordinate-level path.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints are the two named towns given by every source describing this pipeline (Idku origin, Abu Hummus destination), with coordinates taken from each town's own Wikipedia infobox (not fabricated, not GEM-derived). No intermediate waypoints were sourced, so none are given -- lat/lon left null for anything not directly named by a source. Suggested accuracy is 'low' rather than 'medium/high' because only the endpoints, not the pipe's actual path, are sourced.

summary: Real, correctly-classified 30km/42in Idku-to-Abu Hummus gas transmission spur (existence + specs corroborated, though the three text sources share one Presidency-database origin); Owner fields are misattributed -- they are the Idku LNG PLANT's JV ownership (EGPC/EGAS/Shell-BG/Petronas/Engie), not this pipeline's -- and StartYear1=2022 looks like a citation-date mixup for an actual ~2020 completion; FuelSource 'Idku Oil Fields' should be gas fields; no duplicate found in-roster or in GulfPub.
